approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Consumer Data Right) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill is part of a package that would create the Consumer Data Right (CDR), giving individuals and businesses a right to access their data held by businesses and share it with trusted third parties.
The CDR would also require businesses to make public information about specified products they offer.
The explanatory memorandum says a person may commit an offence or face a civil penalty for failing to comply with certain CDR obligations.
Creates a right for individuals and businesses to access and authorise secure sharing of their data held by businesses.
Requires businesses to publicly disclose information on specified products they offer.
Establishes offences and civil penalties for non-compliance with the CDR regime.
Individuals, businesses, and trusted accredited third parties.
